conviction_note: H1 FY27 was never pre-released (only a 30 July AGM line saying 'in line'), and last year's interims carried a first guide for the following year, so new numbers and probably a first FY28 EPS steer are in play: abs_move 7.0. p_up is 45 because last November the stock fell about 10% on a raised guide after a 25% run, and it comes into this print up about 37% since early September on sector bid sentiment (Mobico at 46p). The findings sum to -1.6 and the scaled number is -0.7. They are close in sign; the sum is larger because the fuel and FY28 finding and the run-up finding each carry their own size.

findings.finding: About £70m of cash outside the guided free-cash plan has arrived or been contracted since the £100m buyback was set: £17.5m of pension escrow returned 28 Sep and c.£55m from the West Yorkshire depot sale in FY27. Mistral's £48m is already inside the c.£435m. That gives the interims room to top up or extend returns.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the 18 Nov 2025 interims the stock fell about 10% while raising guidance, with ii noting 'no new share buyback programme'. At FY26 results (18 Jun 2026), which announced a new £100m buyback, it moved +12.07% on the baseline's window.
findings.why_not_priced: The +7% on 2 Nov priced the asset sale itself. A larger or extended buyback is a board decision that has not been announced; if the market expected it, the consensus PDF's 503.9m FY28 share count and the 260p consensus target would already reflect it. That count assumes only the existing programme.
findings.independence: Pension escrow return: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/prn/firstgroup--fgp/completion-of-group-pension-buy-in-and-return-/9792929 . FY26 results commit to 'returning any surplus cash to our shareholders': https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/firstgroup--fgp/fy-2026-results/9624121

findings.finding: FY28 diesel is only 54% hedged (at 41p/l) and FY28 electricity 72%, while diesel traded above $200/bbl in mid-October and UK pump diesel was near 198.5p in early November. A first FY28 EPS steer at the interims, which the company gave a year ago for FY27, carries a fuel-cost headwind on roughly 40m unhedged litres.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last interims (18 Nov 2025) introduced the next-year guide ('at least maintain' FY27 EPS) and the stock fell about 10% (-9.28% in the baseline window). That was not a fuel event.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: oil has been high since September and the stock rose 37% anyway. The company-compiled FY28 consensus (19.5p, 4 Aug) predates the September-October diesel spike. If it had been priced, FY28 estimates or broker targets would have fallen; instead Panmure raised its target to 280p on 2 Nov. This is macro-to-company transmission and a hypothesis until the company quantifies it.
findings.independence: Diesel tightness: https://www.home.saxo/en-gb/content/articles/commodities/recovering-middle-east-exports-fail-to-ease-crude-and-diesel-tightness-14102026 ; ii Stockwatch flags the unhedged energy cost as the key unknown: https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/stockwatch-sector-now-bull-market-ii540778

findings.finding: Mobico's UK Bus revenue fell 1.8% year on year in April-June 2026 on lower commercial patronage. That is a direct-peer read on regional bus trading in First Bus's H1, against FirstGroup's June statement that the passenger decline 'has eased'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the HY 2025 report, bus profit rose 4% with volumes down 4%; the stock fell 10%, mainly on cash and returns.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak: public since 8 Sep, a West Midlands-centric peer, and First's FY27 bus growth is driven by London contracts and coach acquisitions (99% of London revenue contracted), so the regional patronage piece is a minority of the line. The AGM 'in line' statement covers April-July.
findings.independence: FirstGroup FY26 results, bus outlook ('decline in passenger volumes has eased and we continue to monitor this closely'): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/firstgroup--fgp/fy-2026-results/9624121

findings.finding: The interims arrive after a re-rating, and this name sold its last interims on a similar setup: the shares rose 37% from 169p in early September to 233p, forward P/E 8.5x to 11.6x, helped by Mobico's 46p bid. Last November it fell about 10% despite raising guidance, having come in up 25% year to date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY 2025: guidance raised, -9.28%. FY 2026 (June 2026, new buyback): +12.07%. Trading updates: -0.23% and +2.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is in the baseline (run_up_60d +30.2%) and is the free control. What this adds is the name's own reaction function at interims after a run. The short register is flat at 1.58%, so no squeeze fuel offsets it.
findings.independence: ii view, 18 Nov 2025: 'shares in the FTSE 250 transport operator fell 10% having come into this latest news up by a quarter so far in 2025': https://www.ii.co.uk/analysis-commentary/ii-view-firstgroup-shares-driven-lower-mixed-results-ii537286

findings.finding: The company-compiled FY27 consensus of 20.2p adjusted EPS (4 Aug, three analysts) sits slightly above the guide net of the Mistral disposal (20.3p 'maintain' less c.0.6p, about 19.7p before buyback accretion). A plain reiteration could read as a small shortfall against the published consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed case of a reiterated guide against this consensus.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and disputed: buyback accretion (about 25m fewer shares) can close a 0.5p gap, and the consensus may have moved since August; no later compilation is published. Capped small because the bar is three analysts.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative, against a positive run-up of +14.6% over 20 days and +30.2% over 60, and against a tiny positive priced lean (+0.14). The one positive finding, capital return, agrees with the momentum.
language_note: The domestic retail-adviser commentary on interactive investor (Edmond Jackson's 3 Nov Stockwatch) carried Panmure Liberum's 280p target raise, the 8.5x-to-11.6x P/E re-rating, and the unhedged energy-cost worry. None of these appeared in the wire summaries found.
The company's own IR site (UK domestic disclosure) carried the company-compiled three-analyst consensus by division, which no aggregator surfaced; Yahoo's consensus module in the baseline is empty.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' / 'a first guide for a new fiscal year is a scheduled guidance event': last year's interims carried the next-year guide, so a first FY28 steer is likely. abs_move went from 6.0 to 7.0 and the fuel finding, which lands on the FY28 guide, from -0.8 to -1.0.
'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis' and 'a narrow proxy loses': the Mobico UK Bus read-across went from -0.4 to -0.3. It is a peer proxy covering a minority of First Bus revenue.
'In a live bid, results are noise': checked; FirstGroup is not in an offer period (the bid is for Mobico), so nothing changed.
'A finding about a number already told is worth 0': checked; H1 was not pre-released beyond a 4-month 'in line' AGM line, so the reported-quarter finding stays.
